commentary: Seven activities this week versus six last week, which is already the kind of thing that makes me want to climb something and announce it. The run went from 9.0km to 9.6km and you kept the heart rate almost identical at 162 versus 163, which means you ran further for essentially the same effort — that is not nothing, that is genuinely hot. The swim story is a little messier: Monday and Tuesday both came in at 2000m and 146 bpm, consistent and solid, but that Friday morning swim at 901m and 98 bpm reads like you got in the water, looked around, decided that was enough, and climbed back out, which I respect as a lifestyle choice even if it is not exactly training. The weights are showing up reliably across the week and I love that for you, but three sessions in a program still labelled W26-29 suggests we are maybe running a little behind schedule, and I am keeping an eye on that with the same energy I use to watch someone take one too many tequilas at a party — fond, watchful, not yet intervening.
metrics_commentary: Nearly five kilometres in the pool and a solid run on top of that — the body doing all of that work is not a body that needs to apologise for anything, ever, in any room. That HRV sitting at 58 with a seven-day average of 44 tells me recovery is trending in exactly the right direction, which means the engine is actually absorbing what you're throwing at it. VO2 Max at 55.6 is genuinely impressive and I will be bragging about it on your behalf to anyone who will listen. The one thing I want to see next week is more than one run, because that kind of cardiovascular base deserves to be shown off a little more often than once.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which is not four, but let's talk about what actually happened in those three, because a seventeen-kilogram jump on the overhead press e1RM — from 40.0 to 46.7 kilograms — is not a small thing, that is your shoulders announcing themselves. Volume is down dramatically from the previous week at 5,790 kilograms versus 20,753, which is the honest gap and Scott will have thoughts about it, but a PR week is still a PR week. The strength numbers underneath it all — 168.0 on the leg press, 107.9 on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 on the bench — are the body that's being built, session by session, whether the week was tidy or not. Come back for the fourth one next week and watch what happens.
